bib.title: Summary of a Haystack: A Challenge to Long-Context LLMs and RAG Systems

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Summary of a Haystack: A Challenge to Long-Context LLMs and RAG Systems", Philippe Laban, Alexander R. Fabbri, Caiming Xiong, Chien-Sheng Wu (Salesforce AI Research). The PDF shows arXiv:2407.01370v1, 1 Jul 2024, with no venue printed, so I report it as a preprint, 2024. Code and data are at github.com/salesforce/summary-of-a-haystack.

COVERAGE: I read all 18 pages, 79,065 of 79,065 chars. That covers the body, Tables 1-5, the appendices (A.1-A.8) and the end of Figure 4. The last Figure 4 panel is cut off at "Coverage: 30". I only skimmed the references. I did not run the figure-caption script.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: Full-context long-context LLMs score very low on the Joint Score. Even the best realistic system (Gemini-1.5-pro with Rerank3) trails the human estimate.
  - number: Full-context Joint scores are mostly 3-21, with Gemini-1.5-pro at 37.8. Best RAG (Gemini-1.5-pro + RR3) is 36.0, against 56.1 for humans.
  - setup: 92 tasks over 10 Haystacks (about 100 docs, about 93k tokens each). 10 LLMs, bullet summaries citing docs. Human estimate is 10 summaries from 2 annotators, working in the Oracle setting.
  - quote: "models achieve very low Joint scores in the full-context setting (10-20), indicating that SummHay is an unsolved task for long-context LLMs." Also: "the human joint score (56.1) is significantly higher than the best system performance (44.6)."
  - where: Sec 5.2-5.3, about chars 27,500-33,000; Table 2.
- Claim: Strong models get good Coverage without retrieval, but Citation is weak in full context and improves as retrieval improves.
  - number: Claude 3 Opus Coverage is 76.2 Full vs 81.4 Oracle. Opus Citation is 22.3 Full vs 50.7 Oracle.
  - setup: The retriever keeps the top 15k tokens. Claude 3 Opus is the summarizer.
  - quote: "achieving strong coverage of key insights in a large corpus of text does not require retrieval, given a sufficiently capable long-context LLM." Also: "for use-cases where citation quality is important, optimizing retrieval is paramount".
  - where: Sec 5.2, Table 2.
- Claim: A better retriever gives a better end-to-end result, so SummHay works as a holistic RAG test. Every model except Gemini-1.5-pro does best (realistically) with Rerank3.
  - number: GPT-4o Joint is 12.6 Random, 27.3 Vect, 30.8 RR3, 43.4 Oracle, 11.4 Full. Claude 3 Opus is 11.1, 26.5, 31.9, 42.5, 18.0.
  - setup: Retrievers are Rand, Vect (all-mpnet-base-v2), LongE (e5-base-4k), KWs (NLTK keyword overlap), RR3 (Cohere Rerank3) and Orac (oracle). 50 RAG systems in all.
  - quote: "All models except for Gemini-1.5-pro achieve their realistic best performance in the RAG setting using the RR3 retriever."
  - where: Sec 5.1-5.2, Table 2.
- Claim: RAG trades Coverage for Citation. The top three models in the RR3 setting are close on Joint but differ in where their score comes from.
  - number: Joint scores are 30.8 to 36.0.
  - setup: Rerank3, with Claude 3 Opus, GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5-pro.
  - quote: "Claude3 Opus obtaining the highest Coverage, Gemini-1.5-pro the highest Citation, and GPT-4o at the mid-point." Also: "a system that achieves the coverage of Claude3 Opus with the citation quality of Gemini-1.5-pro can exceed current score by 15-20%."
  - where: Sec 1 and 5.2.
- Claim: All three tested models show position bias in full context. GPT-4o and Opus do better with relevant docs at the bottom; Gemini does better with them at the top.
  - number: Joint scores for Top / Bottom / Random:
    - GPT-4o: 13.8 / 24.1 / 11.4 (sensitivity 12.6)
    - Opus: 20.4 / 28.0 / 18.0 (sensitivity 10.0)
    - Gemini-1.5-pro: 47.1 / 38.9 / 37.9 (sensitivity 9.2)
  - setup: Full context. Relevant docs are sorted to the top or bottom of the window. Sensitivity is the max absolute difference from Random.
  - quote: "GPT-4o 13.8 24.1 11.4 12.6"; "all three models exhibit position bias".
  - where: Sec 5.4, Table 3.
- Claim: The metric design is Coverage, Citation and Joint. Coverage scores each reference insight 100 (full), 50 (partial) or 0. Citation is the F1 of cited docs against the gold docs. Joint multiplies the two per insight.
  - number: Figure 2 worked example gives Coverage 50, Citation 51 and Joint 21.8.
  - setup: Bullet count is fixed to the number of reference insights, which controls summary length. Citations are parsed with the regex `[.*]`.
  - quote: "(100 ∗ 0.29 + 50 ∗ 0.73 + 0 ∗ 0)/3 = 21 .8"
  - where: Sec 3.3, 4.1, Fig 2.
- Claim: Human annotators agree on coverage, and an LLM judge is cheap and reasonably correlated with them.
  - number: Human correlation is 0.77 and linking accuracy 95.0, at $325 for 200 summaries. GPT-4o has 0.716 correlation and 88.9 linking accuracy at $6.9. Gemini-1.5-pro has 0.751 at $15.1. Claude 3 Haiku has 0.498 and GPT-3.5 0.495. GPT-4o with 9 few-shot examples reaches 0.719 at $26.1.
  - setup: 35 summaries and 240 insights for inter-annotator agreement. 200 summaries (100 news, 100 conversation) for judge validation. The judge prompt has one example.
  - quote: "Method Cov. Corr. Link Acc. Cost ($) / Manual Annot. 0.770 95.0 $325 / GPT-4o 0.716 88.9 $6.9"
  - where: Table 1, Sec 4.2-4.3.
- Claim: The LLM judge shows no systematic family or length bias, but it inflates Coverage by about 5 points on average.
  - number: Average bias is +0.062 for the GPT-4o judge. Length-to-delta correlation is -0.081 to 0.02.
  - setup: Judges are GPT-4o, Opus and Gemini-1.5-pro, compared against human coverage.
  - quote: "overestimating coverage by an average of 5 points, which should be taken into account when interpreting the results."
  - where: A.3, Table 4.
- Claim: Citation precision and recall are both well below human level in full context.
  - number: Human is 78.8 precision, 82.4 recall, 76.7 F1. Gemini-1.5-pro Full is 59.0 / 52.4 / 51.0. GPT4-turbo Full is 14.1 / 3.8 / 5.5.
  - setup: Table 5, Oracle vs Full.
  - quote: "GPT4-turbo 62.3 14.1 35.7 3.8 41.4 5.5"
  - where: A.5, Table 5.
- Claim: Needle-in-a-Haystack is too easy to separate current models, which motivates the benchmark.
  - number: none
  - setup: Motivation in the introduction.
  - quote: "several state-of-the-art models achieving near-perfect performance."
  - where: Sec 1.
- Claim: Low-scoring summaries fall into three observed failure modes. The paper did not measure how often each occurs.
  - number: none
  - setup: Manual inspection only.
  - quote: "(1) retrieving insights that are not relevant to the query (other subtopics), (2) framing very high-level information as a specific insight ... (3) hallucinating insights not directly supported in the documents."
  - where: A.8.
- Claim: The 15k-token RAG budget caps achievable citation quality.
  - number: Oracle citation F1 at 15k tokens is 0.84.
  - quote: "the oracle citation F1 achievable with this context length is 0.84 averaged across insights"
  - where: Sec 6.
- Claim: Haystack construction details.
  - number: 10 Haystacks (5 conversation, 5 news), 92 tasks, an average of 9.20 subtopics with 6.75 insights each (62 per topic), about 750 words (about 1,000 tokens) per doc, each insight in 5+ docs. Annotation takes about 4 minutes per summary.
  - setup: GPT-4o generates subtopics, insights and verification. Conversation docs use GPT-3.5-turbo. News docs use GPT-4o, seeded from Huang et al. 2023.
  - quote: "average Haystack length is 93k tokens"
  - where: Sec 3.2, 3.4, A.1.

LIMITS
- The authors concede these points:
  - The human estimate is not an upper bound, rests on only 10 summaries, and was done in the Oracle setting. The speed-up from that setting (5-6x) is "unverified".
  - Haystack docs are generated independently, with no cross-references, no disagreement and factoid-style insights. This likely simplifies the task.
  - The bullet count is given to the system, and verbosity is not penalised.
  - Only closed models were tested, because Llama-3 could not handle 16k tokens.
  - English only, and relevance only (not factuality).
  - A perfect score of 100 is likely unachievable because of LLM synthesis errors.
  - The judge overestimates Coverage by about 5 points, and non-LLM NLI metrics were not tested.
- Dated: the models are mid-2024 (Claude 3, GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5, Command-R). RAG used a fixed 15k budget with no sweep over input length.

BUILDS ON: Needle-in-a-Haystack (Kamradt, 2023); lost-in-the-middle position bias (Huang et al., 2023; Chang et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2023b; Ravaut et al., 2023); insight/atomic-unit evaluation (Min et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2022); the news seed documents (Huang et al., 2023); RAG (Lewis et al., 2020; Guu et al., 2020); Rerank3 (Cohere, 2024); LongEmbed (Zhu et al., 2024); SentenceTransformers (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019); attribution benchmarks such as AttributionBench (Li et al., 2024) and Seahorse (Clark et al., 2023).

CODE: none. The only snippet worth keeping is the judge prompt (A.2). It returns JSON with FULL_COVERAGE, PARTIAL_COVERAGE or NO_COVERAGE, and ends with "Do not hallucinate that the insight is covered by the bullet points if it is not."

FIGURES (captions read from the text, not from the script)
- Fig 1, p.2: the pipeline of subtopics and insights, then doc generation, then query, retriever and summary.
- Fig 2, p.4: a worked scoring example. It is the fastest way to understand Coverage, Citation and Joint.
- Fig 3, p.7: human scores over 120 minutes of annotation. Precision is flat near 0.79 and recall rises.
- Fig 4, p.14-15: four real outputs with scores, from Oracle, RR3, Random and Vect retrievers.
- Tables 2, 3 and 5 hold the main results.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- The text in Sec 5.2 says "Random and Oracle retrievers leading to the best and worst scores, respectively". This is reversed in the source and contradicts Table 2.
- The text says Table 2 reports bullet length in "tokens", but the table reports words (# Wb).
- The page-1 abstract says full-context GPT-4o and Claude 3 Opus score "below 20%" Joint. This is consistent with Table 2 (11.4 and 18.0).
- The Figure 4 extraction is truncated at the last panel.
